alex: Heads up — sustained NVMe iops spike in us-central2 (nvme pool shard-7). GPU allocation queue growing, some pod binds failing. Anyone seeing scrub/cleaner cadence change? :eyes:
maria: On it. Which metric graph? any sample node id?
alex: sample from monitoring:
```
[node=us-central2-nvme-7] read_iops=456000 write_iops=22000 avg_lat=14ms fsync_backlog=120 pending_allocs=200
```
tian: That read_iops curve looks like janitor overlap + a firmware requeue. We rolled janitor cadence last night in us-central2 — @ryan any cron changes?
ryan: I pushed a janitor rollout at 02:12 UTC — concurrency went 4->8 for rollout speed. checking logs...
infra-bot: ALERT: nvme_iops_spike detected in us-central2 at 2025-11-02T02:48:01Z — auto-tagged for storage-team
maria: If concurrency doubled that's likely the source. Recommend temporarily scaling janitor concurrency to 2 and pause aggressive scrub on hot shards. Quick patch:
```
PATCH /infra/api/v1/configs/janitor -d '{"concurrency":2}'
```
alex: applied patch against canary config at 1755004389, nodes affected 3/3. iops dropped to ~160k after ~6m. pending_allocs still ~140 though.
tian: Good. Next step: cordon the top 2 hottest nodes and drain their GPU workloads to let cleaner finish without provoking more IOPS. Also add a temporary routing rule: route gpu-allocs away from us-central2-nvme-pool -> ssd-fallback.
maria: I'll open a short-lived rollback ticket for janitor cadence and create a follow-up to capture wear-rate / SMART anomalies. Add a note to incident board: https://redwood.infra/boards/IOPS-1755 :thumbsup:
alex: thanks — keeping an eye. Will post if pending allocs cross 200 again. :coffee:
